fundamentals.summary: Alphabet (GOOGL) presents a healthy and expanding business. 2025 revenues rose to 402.8B with net income of 132.2B and a solid 32% operating margin, supported by a strong 164.7B operating cash flow and 73.3B free cash flow. The balance sheet shows ample liquidity (cash and marketable securities above 126B at year-end 2025, rising further by 9/30/2026) and a modest debt burden (debt-to-equity ~0.12) with a healthy current ratio (~2.0). The company also reports a substantial backlog, especially in Google Cloud (backlog up to 567.7B as of 9/30/2026), signaling improving future revenue visibility. However, a sizable portion of near-term net income gains in 9M 2026 comes from non-operating gains on equity securities, which could mask underlying operating performance and margins. Regulatory and antitrust risks remain material, with multiple ongoing matters and accrued fines noted in the filings, and the company also faces very large future commitments tied to infrastructure, energy, and licensing agreements. Taken together, the core business appears robust and improving, but the near-term profitability and cash flow are sensitive to capital-market-driven gains and regulatory outcomes highlighted in the filings.
